name: Perseverance (Mars 2020)
keyDiscovery: Perseverance found organic molecules and carbonate minerals in the Jezero delta sediments, and MOXIE successfully produced oxygen from Martian CO₂ for the first time.
missionLegacy: Perseverance is caching the first rock samples for return to Earth, and Ingenuity proved powered flight is possible on another planet — opening a new era of aerial Mars exploration.
funFact: Ingenuity, the tiny helicopter that was supposed to fly just five times, ended up making 72 flights — and it carries a small swatch of fabric from the Wright Brothers' 1903 Flyer.
heritageNote: Perseverance continues to operate in Jezero Crater as of 2024; Ingenuity was grounded at Valinor Hills on 18 January 2024 after blade damage on its 72nd flight and now serves as a stationary weather station.

objects.name: Perseverance Rover
objects.description: Perseverance landed on 18 February 2021 in Jezero Crater, a 45-km-wide ancient lake bed. Built on Curiosity's proven design but carrying new instruments, its primary mission is to search for signs of ancient microbial life and collect rock samples for future return to Earth. It also carries MOXIE, which demonstrated making oxygen from Martian CO₂.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Found organic molecules in delta sediments and used MOXIE to produce oxygen from Martian CO₂ — a technology critical for future human missions.
objects.legacy: Still operational and collecting samples for Mars Sample Return; the most advanced astrobiology laboratory ever sent to another planet.
objects.firstPerson: I am the most advanced robot ever sent to another world. I landed in a dried-up lake to search for signs of ancient life, and I am collecting rock samples in sealed tubes for a future mission to bring home. I even carry MOXIE, which breathes Mars's air and makes oxygen. I am paving the way for the first humans on Mars.

objects.name: Ingenuity Helicopter
objects.description: Ingenuity was the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet. Weighing just 1.8 kg, it made 72 flights over nearly three years, far exceeding its planned five-flight technology demonstration. On 18 January 2024, it damaged a rotor blade during its 72nd flight and was retired. It proved that aerial exploration of Mars is possible.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Proved powered, controlled flight is possible in Mars's thin atmosphere (1% of Earth's), scouting terrain for Perseverance and photographing the surface from above.
objects.legacy: Grounded at Valinor Hills since 18 January 2024 after blade damage on flight 72; it now serves as a stationary weather station while still communicating with Perseverance.
objects.firstPerson: I am Ingenuity, and I carry a piece of the Wright Brothers' Flyer inside me. I was supposed to fly just five times — but I flew seventy-two. I soared over Martian dunes, scouted paths for Perseverance, and proved that aircraft can fly on another world. My blade is damaged now and I will never fly again, but I showed the way.

objects.name: Sample Cache Depot
objects.description: Perseverance has collected and sealed rock core samples in titanium tubes, then deposited backup copies at the Three Forks cache depot in Jezero Crater. Ten tubes rest on the surface in a carefully mapped pattern. A future Mars Sample Return mission aims to bring these tubes to Earth — they would be the first samples returned from another planet.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Contains sealed rock cores that may hold biosignatures from an ancient lake — they would be the first samples ever returned from another planet.
objects.legacy: Ten titanium tubes rest on the surface at Three Forks, awaiting a future Mars Sample Return mission to bring them to Earth.
objects.firstPerson: I am ten titanium tubes lying in a careful pattern on the Martian surface. Inside each of us is a core of ancient rock drilled by Perseverance — rock that may hold traces of life from billions of years ago. We are waiting for a future mission to pick us up and fly us to Earth. We could be the most important delivery in human history.

objects.name: Jezero Delta Remnant
objects.description: Jezero Crater contains a well-preserved river delta where a river once flowed into the ancient lake. Perseverance explored the delta and found sedimentary rocks with organic molecules and minerals formed in water. The layered structure preserves evidence of changing water levels and environments over billions of years.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Contains sedimentary rocks with organic molecules and water-formed minerals, preserving billions of years of changing lake environments and possible biosignatures.
objects.legacy: The Jezero delta is one of the most promising places to search for ancient Martian life, and Perseverance's samples from here are the highest-priority targets for Mars Sample Return.
objects.firstPerson: I am the remains of a river delta, three and a half billion years old. A river once flowed into a lake here, carrying sediment and perhaps life. My layers hold organic molecules and minerals born in water. Perseverance drilled into me and sealed my secrets in tubes. One day those tubes will travel to Earth, and scientists will finally read my story.

objects.name: SuperCam Laser Marks
objects.description: SuperCam fires a laser at rocks from up to 7 metres away, vaporising a tiny spot and analysing the flash of light to determine chemical composition. It can also use Raman spectroscopy to identify minerals and organic compounds. The small pits left by the laser on Martian rocks are among the most precise human-made marks on another world.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Analyses rock chemistry from up to 7 metres away using laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy, detecting minerals and organic compounds remotely.
objects.legacy: SuperCam's laser pits on Martian rocks are among the most precise human-made marks on another world; its data guides which rocks Perseverance drills.
objects.firstPerson: I fire a laser that vaporises a tiny spot of rock from seven metres away, then I read the flash of light to learn what that rock is made of. I can also use Raman spectroscopy to find organic molecules. I have zapped hundreds of targets across Jezero Crater. Every tiny pit I leave is a question answered about Mars's history.

objects.name: Descent Stage Wreckage
objects.description: Like Curiosity, Perseverance was lowered to the surface by a sky crane. The descent stage then flew 700 metres away and crashed. HiRISE orbital images show the dark debris field. Perseverance's cameras captured the first video of a Mars landing, showing the parachute deployment, heat shield separation, and sky crane sequence in stunning detail.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Perseverance's EDL cameras captured the first-ever video of a Mars landing, providing engineering data that will improve future landings.
objects.legacy: The debris field is visible from orbit; the landing video became one of the most-watched space exploration videos in history.
objects.firstPerson: I lowered Perseverance to the ground on cables, then flew away and crashed — just like my twin did for Curiosity. But this time, cameras recorded everything. Millions of people watched me work in the first-ever video of a Mars landing. I may be wreckage now, but that footage will inspire engineers for generations.
